$comment: [X4.5] MongoDB MCP attach spec. Tier-2 VERIFIED-PUBLISHER (publisher `mongodb-js` — official MongoDB MCP server from github.com/mongodb-js; X1.x evidence). Shape === mcp-specs/_template.json (X2.1). Database + Atlas tooling; HAS destructive drop/delete tools (see destructive_tools + X2.18 audit). CC0-1.0.
title: MongoDB Database & Atlas
description: Query MongoDB collections and administer Atlas clusters — find, aggregate, schema inference, and cluster operations — via the official MongoDB MCP server.

env_vars.name: MDB_MCP_CONNECTION_STRING
env_vars.description: MongoDB connection string for a direct database connection (local or Atlas). Optional — if unset, call the `connect` tool first. Pass via env, never inline in args (doctrine #6).

env_vars.name: MDB_MCP_API_CLIENT_ID
env_vars.description: Atlas service-account client ID. Required only to enable the Atlas administration tools (`atlas-*`).

env_vars.name: MDB_MCP_API_CLIENT_SECRET
env_vars.description: Atlas service-account client secret. Required only to enable the Atlas administration tools; pass via env, never inline in args (doctrine #6).

env_vars.name: MDB_MCP_READ_ONLY
env_vars.description: Set to `true` to restrict the server to read/connect/metadata tools (equivalent to the `--readOnly` flag); disables all create/update/delete tools.

auth.recipe: set MDB_MCP_CONNECTION_STRING to connect to a database (or call the `connect` tool), and/or set MDB_MCP_API_CLIENT_ID + MDB_MCP_API_CLIENT_SECRET (an Atlas service account) to enable the Atlas tools; prefer a least-privilege user/key.

sample_tools.name: find
sample_tools.summary: Run a find query against a MongoDB collection.

sample_tools.name: aggregate
sample_tools.summary: Run an aggregation pipeline against a collection.

sample_tools.name: count
sample_tools.summary: Count documents in a collection matching a filter.

sample_tools.name: list-databases
sample_tools.summary: List all databases for the active connection.

sample_tools.name: list-collections
sample_tools.summary: List all collections in a database.

sample_tools.name: collection-schema
sample_tools.summary: Infer and describe a collection's schema.

sample_tools.name: atlas-list-clusters
sample_tools.summary: List MongoDB Atlas clusters in a project.

known_limitations: Without MDB_MCP_CONNECTION_STRING (or Atlas credentials) the server starts but exposes no data until you call the `connect` tool with a connection string.
The Atlas administration tools (`atlas-*`) only register when Atlas service-account credentials (MDB_MCP_API_CLIENT_ID / MDB_MCP_API_CLIENT_SECRET) are set.
Write and admin tools operate against real data — pass `--readOnly` (or MDB_MCP_READ_ONLY=true) to attach in safe read-only mode for analysis.

Destructive-action audit (X2.18): delete-many, drop-collection, drop-database, and drop-index are flagged in `destructive_tools` and are blocked when the trust policy sets `allowDestructive: false` (MongoDB also gates them behind elicitation confirmation).

client_install.claude_desktop: Add to claude_desktop_config.json mcpServers as `mongodb`: { command: npx, args: [-y, mongodb-mcp-server, --readOnly], env: { MDB_MCP_CONNECTION_STRING: "mongodb+srv://..." } }.
client_install.cursor: Settings → MCP → Add: name `mongodb`, command `npx -y mongodb-mcp-server --readOnly`; set MDB_MCP_CONNECTION_STRING in the env.
client_install.vscode: Add to .vscode/mcp.json servers as `mongodb` (VS Code Insider, MCP preview); supply MDB_MCP_CONNECTION_STRING via inputs.
